claims.statement: Capex plan of INR200-300 crore in FY26 and INR300-400 crore in FY27, totaling INR600-700 crore over next 3 years
Management targets 15-20% CAGR growth over the next many years
Committed capex of $24 million for Nusantara acquisition in FY25-26
Second OSV purchase facing delivery issues, advance deposit in escrow
HAL Offshore newbuild vessel may be transferred to Seamec per promoter consolidation philosophy
Consolidated EBITDA grew 33% YoY to INR81 crores in Q1 FY25
Standalone EBITDA grew 44% YoY to INR86 crores in Q1 FY25
No order book maintained; business runs on confirmed contracts with seasonal deployment
India oilfield services market projected 14% CAGR FY2024-FY2031
Target ROC 18-20% by FY26
Q2 margins lower due to monsoon season reducing deployment to 51%
Expect positive margin increment year-on-year going forward
Three vessels (Seamec-3, Princess, Swordfish) up for repricing in H2 FY25
Seamec-3 completed 20-day charter with Supreme Hydro Engineering in Oct-Nov 2024
Seamec Glorious started second fair-weather season with ONGC on 16 Oct 2024
Seamec Princess remobilized for third season of Pipeline Replacement Project 7 with ONGC in early Nov 2024
Actively looking to acquire vessels in overseas markets
Dry dock completed for Swordfish, Princess and Glorious Barge; Swordfish getting ready for deployment
Maritime Development Fund Rs 25,000 crore with up to 49% government contribution
BCD exemption on shipbuilding raw materials extended 10 years
Seamec Swordfish commenced a 50-day charter with Maritime Mermaid Subsea Services in Saudi Arabia with a firm order value of $3.46 million.
Management believes the worst is behind and the company will be on a growth trajectory from here onwards.
Seeking board approval to acquire Seamec Anant from parent HAL Offshore at $70 million; vessel built in 2023 with 23 years remaining life; acquisition expected to complete by Q2 FY26.
NPP Nusantara acquisition signed; delivery expected around July-August, completion targeted in Q2 FY26; vessel comes with contract in hand and will be EPS accretive from day one.
PEARL acquisition is on pause due to issues with the seller; management is rethinking the deal.
Total capex for two vessels (Anant and Nusantara) estimated at INR800 crores plus dry dock expenses; peak debt not expected to exceed INR500 crores next year with repayment in subsequent years.
Seamec Swordfish secured a 2-year charter; most vessels now on minimum 2-year contracts, only Glorious Barge renewing next year.
Two dry docks planned this year for Seamec Paladin and Seamec II; dry docks factored into contract planning to minimize disruption.
Confident next quarter will be much better as all vessels deployed; FY27 to see full-year contribution from Nusantara and Anant; sustainable growth journey expected over next 3 years.
Board approved purchase of NPP Nusantara (built 2010, 4750 GT) for USD 23 million via debt and internal accruals
Board approved purchase of MSV NPP Nusantara built in 2010 at $23 million financed by mix of debt and internal resources
Seamec Swordfish secured 2-year charter at $78,000 per day effective 21st May 2025
Entire fleet deployed except Barge Glorious off-hire during monsoon 15th May to 15th October
Expect FY26 to be better than FY25 with new vessel Nusantara addition and full fleet deployment
Consolidated EBITDA FY25 INR 244 crores vs INR 271 crores FY24; standalone EBITDA FY25 INR 264 crores vs INR 290 crores FY24
Nusantara acquisition on track to commence operations from Dec'25
HAL Anant acquisition approved by shareholders, expected completion by Oct'25
Management declined to provide revenue or margin guidance for FY26, citing business volatility and suggesting investors refer to research reports.
Fleet largely contracted for next 2-4 years; Paladin 3 years, Swordfish 2 years, Nusantara and Anant 3-4 years, Seamec 2 till March 2026, Seamec 3 and Princess on spot, barge Glorious 7 months/year.
Nusantara acquisition expected to close in August 2025, vessel deployed from December 2025 after dry dock. Seamec Anant acquisition expected to close by October 2025.
Support vessels expected to generate 30-35% margins.
Q1 fleet efficiency 93%; Seamec Princess completed PRP VII early adding 18 revenue days; Seamec 2 dry dock completed 20 days ahead of schedule (by Sept 10).
MOU with Directorate General of Shipping for capex of INR 1,000 crore
MOU with HAL Offshore for charter hire of MV Goodman for ONGC NLM9 project
Seamec Princess commenced PRP VIII project and signed addendum for additional work
Charter hire of Seamec Glorious with L&T for firm 150 days with extension option
Net debt expected at INR300-400 crores by March 31, 2026
Seamec Glorious secured 150-day charter with L&T for Mumbai High and Western Offshore
Charter hire agreement worth INR6.3 crores signed with HAL Offshore for vessel GOODMAN
MoU signed with DG Shipping to invest approximately INR1,000 crores in maritime business over next few years
Seamec Agastya acquired for $23 million (~INR200 crores) with expected IRR upwards of 20%
Seamec Anant mobilization planned by February 1, 2026 after shareholder approval for RPT transaction
Seamec Agastya scheduled for deployment from December 2025 on 4-year ONGC contract at USD25,000/day via HAL Offshore
Nusantara at USD25,000/day and Anant at USD45,000/day, both on 4-year ONGC contracts
Three vessels (Seamec-3, Seamec Princess, Seamec Paladin) planned for dry dock in 2026; Seamec-2, SWORDFISH, Nusantara in FY27-28
Higher margins post-COVID due to increased charter rates, shift to higher-margin IMR contracts, and younger fleet with lower maintenance
New MSV construction takes 2.5-3 years; replacement cost ~$100 million per vessel; fleet theoretical value INR1,500-1,800 crores
Charter rates expected to prevail for next 4-5 years; potential for higher rates with further service additions
Natural gas consumption forecast CAGR 4.59% to 500 MT by FY40
Crude oil consumption forecast 7.2 MBPD by 2030, 9.2 MBPD by 2050
Refining capacity additions 56 MTPA by 2028 to reach 310 MTPA
Management expects charter rates to remain steady and sustainable for some more time with steady revenue visibility from mix of long-term and short-term contracts
MOU signed with DG Shipping for INR1,000 crores investment over next 2-3 years for acquisition of one or more vessels
Seamec Anant vessel acquisition expected to complete in Q4 FY26 with deployment in Q1 FY27
Seamec Paladin undergoing dry docking for approximately 70 days from Q4 FY26
Three vessels (Seamec III, Seamec Princess, Seamec Glorious) scheduled for dry docking in FY27 during monsoon period with minimal revenue disruption
IMR contracts provide higher margins and full-year deployment versus EPC contracts which have monsoon off-hire periods
Swordfish vessel expected to work full year in FY27 versus partial year in FY26; Agastya and Anant additions will drive growth
Capital expenditure Rs 22.6735 crore
SEAMEC II contract extended by ONGC through August 2026
Received Notification of Award for O&M services for ONGC MSV Samudra Prabha and Samudra Sevak 2026-2028 in consortium
Fleet comprises 6 DSVs, 1 OSV, 1 accommodation barge, 2 bulk carriers
Management guided for ~15% top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 with EBITDA margin in the 40-42% range.
CFO reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of ~15% and stable EBITDA margin of 40-42% despite Paladin off-hire.
Two O&M contracts (MSV Samudra Prabha and Samudra Sevak) awarded in consortium with Supreme Hydro, tenure 2026-2028, Seamec holds 90% share.
FY26 capex ~Rs.300 cr; FY27 scheduled capex ~$70 mn for Seamec Anant acquisition.
Seamec Agastya integrated and commenced operations; Seamec Anant expected to join fleet in one more quarter; Seamec Paladin stuck in Dubai due to Strait of Hormuz closure.
Vessel utilization near 100% barring dry-dock/off-hire; three own vessels plus two O&M vessels due for dry-dock in FY27.
Proposed acquisition of SEAMEC Anant from HAL Offshore to be completed in Q2 FY27
Fleet comprises 6 DSVs, 1 OSV, 1 accommodation barge, 1 bulk carrier
SEAMEC Agastya acquired and commenced operations in FY26
SEAMEC Diamond resumed operations after statutory dry docking
India PSU oil sector capex expected to increase to Rs 1.3-1.4 lakh crore with growing offshore share
Government approved Samudra Manthan scheme with Rs 84,084 crore outlay through FY2030-31
Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years
Annual EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 40-42%
Seamec ANANT acquisition completing end of July, will resume ONGC IMR contract after ~1 month statutory formalities
Seamec Princess and Seamec III off-hire for monsoon; advanced talks for new contracts from October
Seamec ANANT purchase consideration USD 70 million, financed 50-50 internal equity and loans
Gallant vessel sale expected to complete in September post shareholder approval
MOU with DG Shipping for INR 1,000 crore fleet growth over 2 years remains active; ANANT acquisition is first step
Seamec ANANT expected 95-98% utilization once deployed on IMR contract
Paladin vessel returned from Dubai dry dock and resumed operations in Q2
Seamec II charter ending August; evaluating redeployment for EPC work
Seamec Glorious barge remains off-hire during monsoon along with Princess and Seamec III
Acquired SEAMEC Anant for USD 70 Mn in Oct 2026
SEAMEC Anant long-term charter ~1,225 days ~USD 55 Mn with ONGC for IMR
Fleet now 7 DSVs 1 OSV 1 accommodation barge 1 bulk carrier
Government approved Samudra Manthan Rs 84,084 crore through FY2030-31
Seamec Anant taken over on 14 Oct 2026 and signed 1,225-day charter with HAL Offshore for ONGC IMR work at ~USD 55 million contract value
H1 FY27 capex of $70 million for Seamec Anant acquisition; plan $200-250 million capex over next 2-3 years for fleet expansion
Medium-term guidance of ~15% revenue CAGR and ~18-20% PAT CAGR over next 4-5 years; stable-state EBITDA margin ~40% for next 3-4 years
Guiding ~40% EBITDA margins on stable state for next 3-4 years; quarterly volatility due to monsoon will persist but taper over time
Swordfish dry dock scheduled in FY27-28; all other vessels dry docked in FY27; Seamec Princess out of dry dock and in advanced talks with L&T for PRP-X contract
New build DSV cost $110-150 million; second-hand acquisition preferred if accretive; new build also in pipeline as fleet expansion option
4 vessels on seasonal spot contracts (Nov-May); rest on long-term charters; Sevak, Prabha, Swordfish charters up for renewal next year
Seamec Anant acquired at $70 million vs open market value $80-90 million; payback ~5-6 years; plan to bid directly to ONGC after 3-year HAL charter
